en: The Twenty-one Praises:
Homage to Tārā! O Heroine, swift one, whose eyes resemble the flash of lightning, born from the filaments blooming in the lotus-face of the Lord of the Three Worlds.
Homage to you, O Tārā, whose face is like a full orb of the autumn moon in its tranquility,
blazing with thousands of rays that shine with a smile;
homage to you, adorned with lotus-hands holding a golden-blue lotus.
Homage to the one whose sphere is generosity, vigor, austerity, patience, endurance, and meditation; to the Tathāgata-uṣṇīṣa-vijayā who wanders infinitely;
she who is served by the sons of the Conquerors who have attained all the perfections without exception.
Homage to her who fills the quarters and the reaches of space with the syllables *namaḥ*, *tuttāra*, and *hūṃ*;
who, in the instant of summoning all without exception, has stepped upon the seven worlds;
homage to her worshipped by Śakra, humans, Brahmā, the Maruts, and the lords of the universe.
Homage to her who is preceded by hosts of spirits, vetālas, and gandharvas;
to her who possesses the *trāt*, *tritri*, and *phaṭ* syllables, the crusher of supreme mantras;
to her whose placement of feet is in the *pratyālīḍha* stance, blazing and radiant with masses of fire-flames.
Homage to you, O Ture, the Great Terrible One, destroyer of the heroes of Māra;
you who have a lotus-face with a frowning brow, the slayer of all the wicked!
Homage to you, marked with the seal of the Three Jewels, adorned with fingers upon the heart!

Homage to her who fills the entire expanse of all directions with her ornaments, amidst the assembly of noble lineages; to her who casts aside the essence [of existence] with the pride of the "Joyful" (Pramuditā) crown;
to Tārā, who laughs and laughs aloud, striking terror into the world of Māra.
Homage to her who, in an instant, draws down all the kings of the earth and the netherworld;
who utters the syllable *hūṃ* with a frown, and who liberates one from all calamities.
Homage to her who blazes with the ornament of a crown of crescent moons and crests.
Homage to her who possesses the splendor of Amitābha, radiant and steady with rays of light; homage to her who strikes the earth with the palm of her hand and stamps it with her feet,
and who destroys the seven underworlds with the *hūṃ* uttered from her furrowed brow.

Homage to her who stands amidst the garlands of flames of the fire at the end of the eon; who, established in the *ālīḍha* posture, brings about the destruction of the circle of enemies with joyful resolve. Homage to Śivā, the auspicious and peaceful one, whose sphere is the peace of nirvāṇa.

Svāhā! Salutation to you who are joined with the prostration, the destroyer of great sins. Homage to you who rend the bodies of enemies bound by joy, you who are illumined by the *vidyā* syllable *huṃ* in the placement of the ten-syllable feet.
Homage to Ture, whose life-force is the syllable *huṃ*, who strikes with her feet,
and who traverses Mount Meru, Maṇḍala, Kailāśa, and the three worlds!
Homage to her who stands with hands like those of a lioness devouring gods and asuras!
Homage to you who utter the *phaṭ* syllable twice, the destroyer of all obstacles;
homage to you who are served by hosts of gods, yakṣas, asuras, and kinnaras;
you who produce the enjoyment of bound joy and the destroyer of bad dreams.
Homage to you, who are radiant with the natural luster of eyes filled with the moon and sun;
O Tārā, who are uttered twice for the sake of supreme rescue, and who destroy uneven fires.
Homage to you, who are established in the three levels and endowed with Śiva and Śakti.
O supreme one, who destroys planets, vetālas, yakṣas, and the like, O swift one!
This hymn of twenty-one salutations, which has the mantra as its root, should be recited mostly by the wise person who is endowed with devotion to the Goddess. (1)
Therefore, having risen early in the morning, he should remember this [mantra], which bestows fearlessness upon all, pacifies all sins, and destroys all miserable rebirths;
having attained greatness in this world, he will quickly be consecrated as a lord of both worlds.
His most terrible poison is brought to destruction by mere remembrance.
For those afflicted by the blazing poisons of planetary influences and for other beings as well,
one who desires a son shall obtain a son, and he shall attain all his desires.
Through seven crores of Victors, he shall at the end attain the state of a Buddha;
for this [mantra] indeed destroys all suffering, whether stationary or moving,
and the supreme agony of those who have lived for two, three, or seven [lifetimes].
One who desires wealth shall obtain wealth and shall not be thwarted by obstacles.
Thus ends the twenty-one-fold hymn of praise to the Noble Goddess Tārā, spoken by the Blessed One, the Perfectly Awakened Vairocana. May it be auspicious!
